title: Strongly Secure Symmetric-Key Proxy Re-Encryption from Symmetric-Key Encryption
summary: The source identifies a public-key consequence for any such construction, but whether it can be built from symmetric-key encryption remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Can strongly secure symmetric-key proxy re-encryption be constructed from symmetric-key encryption?

scope.domain: Design of symmetric-key cryptographic primitives, specifically proxy re-encryption and its security.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether symmetric-key encryption can yield symmetric-key proxy re-encryption satisfying the stronger indistinguishability-based security definitions.

progress.summary: The paper poses this question after discussing stronger security definitions for symmetric-key proxy re-encryption. It presents a consequence through ciphertext-independent updatable encryption and public-key encryption, but the supplied evidence gives neither a construction nor an impossibility theorem.
citation_labels: Navid Alamati et al., Symmetric Primitives with Structured Secrets
